main_text.p: Pergit: De lapsu Adami, peccati primi enormitate amissa imagine Dei, & effectis lapsus.
Ego sane quid his velit, ut ingenue fa-tear, non capio, nec quorsum collimat, scio; cum nihil aliud de his sentiant Orientales, quam quod Ecclesia Romana.

Paradoxum hoc est Hottingeri in suorum Reformatorum gratiam, nimirum Caluini in cap. 15, Act. & 2. Institut. cap. 17. Bezæ 2. par. Respon. ad acta Colloq. Montisbel, Piscatoris in thes. lib. 2., & aliorum, nuper in Oriente a Hottingero excogitatum, cum in nostro nullum eiusmodi impium dogma habeatur, solumque dicant, ad id requiri fidem tanquam radicem, & gratiam tanquam adiutricem; proinde passim ita

p.i: Da nobis Domine noster gratiam tuam, ut seruiemus omnia præcepta tua.

main_text.p: Pergit: De Iustificatione, qua absque verborum involucris ita proponitur, ut peccatori omnis gratiæ fons in Christi merito fi-

page.notes: The two lines after "Deum deprecantur:" are in an Oriental script (probably Syriac or Arabic letters), not Greek or Hebrew. I could not read them letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The Latin prayer below them is italic. The first word of the page is a fragment from the previous page and is kept as such. The hyphens in "fa-tear", "impossibi-litate" and the final "fi-" are printed line-end hyphens.
